CLAUDE.md

Source: CLAUDE.md

This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.

Shared conventions

The portfolio’s shared rules are synced into .claude/shared/ from pedrobtz/packages:claude/shared/. Never edit them here. Where this file and a shared file disagree, this file wins for this package.

@.claude/shared/workflow.md @.claude/shared/r-package.md @.claude/shared/ci.md @.claude/shared/native-code.md @.claude/shared/correctness.md @.claude/shared/assurance.md

What this is

qio reads and writes Apache Parquet files from R through the vendored C library carquet. Whole files are read with one call; larger ones can be opened to inspect their schema and read selected columns, row groups or batches. The default API has no required runtime R dependencies (only utils); optional result modes may use suggested packages such as bit64 and hms. Building needs GNU make and system zlib; zstd and LZ4 are bundled, and Rtools supplies zlib on Windows.

Before changing behaviour, read the document that owns it. They outrank this file:

  • .agents/TYPES.md for Parquet-to-R mappings and conversion contracts.
  • .agents/roadmap.md for the current API, release scope and priorities.
  • .agents/plan.md for the ordered v0.1.0 work and exit gates.
  • .agents/VENDORED.md before touching vendored code.
  • .agents/carquet.md for the integration with the vendored carquet snapshot, and .agents/read-performance.md for read performance against nanoparquet.
  • bench/README.md for the benchmark method, workloads, regression threshold and recorded baseline.

.agents/research_arrow_nested/ is background research; where it conflicts with TYPES.md or roadmap.md, those win. AGENTS.md carries the older, self-contained version of these rules for other agents; this file supersedes it for Claude Code.

Current state

Version 0.1.1 is on CRAN (published 2026-09-29); the default branch is 0.1.1.9000, verified 2026-11-11. Since 0.1.1, write_parquet() writes binary, GEOMETRY and GEOGRAPHY columns with geospatial statistics, and geospatial_statistics() reports them; see NEWS.md.

Versions and dependents

The current version’s parent issue is #18 (v0.1.2). Sibling packages that depend on this one before CRAN does: zugeo (Suggests: qio (>= 0.1.1.9000), with Remotes: pedrobtz/qio).

Commands

Beyond the shared commands:

Rscript -e 'devtools::load_all(debug = FALSE)'       # compile at -O2
Rscript -e 'devtools::test(filter = "parquet-plan")' # focused tests
Rscript -e 'pkgdown::check_pkgdown()'                # reference index
Rscript -e 'pkgbuild::clean_dll()'                   # real build reset
Rscript tools/check-inspection-against-arrow.R       # after any rename
tools/check-vendor-drift.sh                          # vendored tree vs pins
tools/check-header-deps.sh                           # header rebuilds

Two things about load_all() worth knowing before trusting a build:

  • It compiles at -O0. Never time anything built with it. Pass debug = FALSE for -O2, or install. See bench/README.md.
  • It decides whether to compile from qio.so, not from the object files. Deleting src/*.o alone leaves the library in place, so load_all() skips compiling and silently keeps whatever flags built it. Use pkgbuild::clean_dll() for a real reset.

src/Makevars* declares vendored headers as prerequisites, so a header change rebuilds every object on its own; tools/check-header-deps.sh proves it. A manual clean is a valid reset but no longer required.

Gate a performance change on bench/benchmark.R --compare on a quiet machine, not on CI numbers.

Architecture

The layers are R API -> package-owned C glue -> vendored C libraries.

  • R/parquet.R: eager I/O and user-facing helpers.
  • R/parquet-file.R: open handles, inspection, selection and collection.
  • R/parquet-plan.R: shared read mapping and logical conversion.
  • R/parquet-schema.R: writer schema inference and overrides.
  • src/qio.c: writer bridge and native registration.
  • src/qio_file.c: handles, metadata, collection and batches.
  • src/qio_path.c: path handling.
  • src/{carquet,zstd,lz4}/: vendored libraries.

read_parquet() is open_parquet() plus collect(). Open files are external pointers with finalizers. Eager reads request mmap and may decode numeric columns in parallel. Persistent handles default to buffered I/O.

Invariants that are easy to break

  • Physical decoding in C, logical reinterpretation in the shared R read plan. qio_type_registry() owns physical fallbacks; qio_apply_plan() must keep read_parquet(), collect() and walk_batches() consistent.
  • Handles. Native entry points must validate the external pointer and respect the open/busy guards; close must stay idempotent.
  • Renaming anything public means a sweep of the whole repository, not of R/ and tests/. bench/, tools/, README.md, AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, .agents/ and C comments all name public functions and result columns, and none of them is compiled or tested, so a stale reference there survives a green suite and a clean R CMD check. tools/check-inspection-against-arrow.R is the one that fails loudly; run it after any rename.
  • Native changes are platform-sensitive. ARM64 uses NEON; typical x86 builds use scalar fallbacks. Windows has its own code paths: code-page path handling with its mmap fallback, and the per-thread zstd context that only ever broke there.
  • NEWS.md. Every user-visible change gets a short NEWS.md item now that 0.1.0 has shipped. (Before 0.1.0 the rule was the opposite: the section stayed * Initial release..)
  • Style deviation: package-owned C uses four-space indentation; R uses two. Internal R helpers are prefixed qio_, and R uses base pipes (|>).

Testing

  • Mirror R/foo.R with tests/testthat/test-foo.R.
  • Interoperability fixtures live under tests/testthat/parquet/, with provenance in the adjacent SOURCE.md. The tools/generate-* scripts build them.
  • helper-warnings.R: collect_warnings() captures every warning an expression raises, with its value, because expect_warning() consumes only one and the per-column coercion warnings need counting.
  • helper-wkb.R: little-endian ISO WKB builders for test geometries.
  • tools/check-writer-against-arrow.R and tools/check-inspection-against-arrow.R cross-check against arrow.
  • .covrignore leaves src/carquet, src/zstd and src/lz4 out of coverage, because they outnumber the package’s own C fifty to one. Package-owned src/qio*.c is deliberately counted.

Continuous integration

  • R-CMD-check.yaml: deviation, still a hand-rolled r-lib/actions matrix rather than a call to r-actions’ r-cmd-check.yml, so it does not yet count as the pre-submission check; #16 tracks the adoption. It runs Windows R-devel on every commit because of the Windows-only paths above.
  • native-checks.yml: r-actions’ sanitizers, Valgrind, LTO and rchk. Pull requests run a quick profile: UBSan without the ASan containers or Valgrind.
  • gctorture.yml: its own workflow, run only when src/** changes (vendored trees included), because it costs about nine times the other native jobs combined. Pull requests run gctorture at step 500 instead of 20. Dispatch it by hand for a release or for a change that alters how C is called without changing C.
  • Deviation from ci.md: label a pull request full-ci to run the full set before merging, and pushes to main always run the full profile, not the quick one.
  • vendor.yml: src/carquet must be exactly the pinned commit of the fork’s qio branch, that branch the upstream pin plus one commit per ledger entry, and a shared vendored header change must rebuild every object.
  • benchmark.yml: publishes benchmark and compare-readers tables and CSVs on every run. It does not gate on performance; it fails only on --max-seconds.
  • coverage.yaml: r-actions’ coverage. pkgdown.yaml: the site.
  • #24 tracks gating jobs on documentation-only pull requests.

Vendored native code

Pins, licences, the patch ledger and the re-vendoring procedure are in .agents/VENDORED.md: carquet v0.6.0 (MIT) via the pedrobtz/carquet fork’s qio branch, zstd v1.5.7 (BSD-3-Clause), lz4 v1.10.0 (BSD-2-Clause).

Never edit src/carquet in place. qio vendors it from the qio branch of the carquet fork, where every local change is its own commit on top of a pinned upstream commit. Make the change there, push it, re-copy, and update the fork pin in .agents/VENDORED.md, which also documents how a patch becomes an upstream pull request. tools/check-vendor-drift.sh fails CI on a vendored file edited in place, and on a ledger that disagrees with the series. The same rule applies to src/zstd and src/lz4: re-vendor rather than patch.

Deviation from native-code.md: the fork’s commit series, not tools/patches/ and src/vendor/PROVENANCE, is the patch record, and the vendored trees sit directly under src/.

Open vendoring work:

  • #4 re-vendor carquet to v0.7.x;
  • #5 fail when the fork’s CI is red at the pin;
  • #6 guard carquet_column_set_preserve_dictionary();
  • #7 upstream the remaining patches;
  • #8 re-benchmark the performance patches against v0.7.0;
  • #17 take zstd and lz4 from zukomp.
